:::{#exm-bilinear-form}
#### A bilinear form that depends on the order of its vectors

<!-- no-figure: the example computes two numbers from one small matrix -->

Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\vx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\vy = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

The bilinear form (@def-bilinear-form) of $\matr{A}$ at $\vx$ and $\vy$ is

$$
\ba
\bform{\matr{A}}{\vx}{\vy}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 3 + 2 \cd (-1) \\ 0 \cd 3 + 3 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vy \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd (-3)
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= -5.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

With the vectors swapped, it is

$$
\ba
\bform{\matr{A}}{\vy}{\vx}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 2 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 3 \cd 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vx \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 3 \cd 5 + (-1) \cd 6
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= 9.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

The two orders give different values.

:::
